questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibilities to go out and explore the nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - Reykjavik University has a lot of information for exchange students on their webside and an international office, which you can e-mail and ask questions and they usually reply very fast.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had arranged a couple of orientation days, where we got a lot of practical information and got attached to tutors, who we could also ask questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, as I started looking for housing early. In general, I would recommend to start searching for accommodation as soon as possible. I found my housing through HousingAnywhere, others used Airbnb or even Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live off campus, you can live closer to the city center with all the shops, grocery stores, cafes, clubs, restaurants, bars, city pools, etc. The rest of Reykjavik, including the area around the university, can seem a little desolate, but it might be cheaper and with more space around you, so it depends on what you value. In any case, if you live off campus, just make sure that you don't book a place too far away from campus and that you can get there by walking, biking and/or public transportation, when the weather is bad. All in all, both the on and off campus housing opportunities was nice and the on campus housing weren't too far from the city center either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found my courses in the university's course calender and applied for them in Reykjavik University's Mobility Online.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always e-mail the international office at the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure to keep the deadlines and don't be afraid to ask questions to the international office.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very much the same level as of UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very much the same as UCPH. However, we had to prepare presentations and write essays, which would count in our final grade, during the semester instead of just being graded on one final exam at the end of the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Law and Economics
US litigation
US legal system: Sources and Structure
European Convention of Human Rights
Principles of Energy Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them - the teaching was good and the workload was managable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Public transportation out of the city was very expensive and limited, why we had to rent a car and pay for fuel + parking everytime we wanted to go on a trip. Also some groceries was more expensive than I thought.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Cheese, meat and some vegetables was more expensive than I thought. Joining a gym was also crazy expensive, so that I didn't prioritize.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university didn't really offer any non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a handfull of academic student associations, but you had to pay to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the citypools, it's where the locals go and it's a nice and cheap thing to do with your friends or just by yourself. There is also a park called Klambratún, where you can meet up and play ball or disc golf.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: To rent a car and get out of the city to do some hikes in the spectacular nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to the ones in your class or join a student association.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The fascination and respect the locals had for the nature and the environment.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be prepared to spend money. It's just an expensive country.
2. Don't worry about making friends, everyone is eager to meet new people and there will be a lot of events arranged by other students. Just be approachable and say yes.
3. Don't be afraid to take initiative yourself if there is something you want to do and be inviting.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It can be helpfull to have researched a bit in advance what you would like to see or do, so you can prioritize your money on that. But you can also decide on that when you have arrived and maybe talked to some of the other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from different countries with different backgrounds and to explore the crazy Icelandic nature together with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To accept that everything was so expensive and having to prioritize my money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I really enjoyed not bringing my work, as it meant that I was more free and not stressed.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
